statements.statement: SEDP builtin writers announce local publications and subscriptions to newly discovered peers.
SEDP publications reader processes DiscoveredWriterData and updates discovery state.
SEDP subscriptions reader processes DiscoveredReaderData and updates discovery state.

Every compatible writer-reader pair that involves a local endpoint is reported once, including a remote endpoint announced before the local one existed; pairs of two remote endpoints are never reported.
Topic and type names are compared whole: an endpoint whose name does not fit RTPS_MAX_TOPIC_NAME_LEN - 1 is ignored rather than matched by its truncated prefix.

When the remote endpoint table, its origin table, or its locator lists are full, an announced endpoint that completes a match with a local endpoint displaces stored remote endpoints that are in no match; an endpoint that completes none is not kept, and a stored endpoint that is part of a match is never displaced.

A local endpoint's topic and type names are kept whole in a shared arena of RTPS_LOCAL_NAME_BYTES, each distinct name stored once however many endpoints use it; they read back exactly after other endpoints are removed or renamed, and an endpoint the table has no record or name room for is not recorded.

A remote endpoint keeps at most RTPS_MAX_REMOTE_ENDPOINT_LOCATORS of the locators it announced: the most reachable UDP locators against the local addresses and prefixes, in announced order within a reachability class, chosen from every locator the announcement lists however many precede the most reachable one; locator kinds the stack cannot send to are not kept.

A remote endpoint that announces no unicast locators, or locators whose preferred entry is its participant's preferred default unicast locator as the SPDP peer table keeps them, keeps no locator list and is reached at its participant's current defaults, including while a peer reactivated from its known-peer record holds only that preferred default; only an endpoint whose preferred locator is elsewhere keeps its locators, in one of RTPS_MAX_REMOTE_LOCATOR_LISTS lists; an endpoint moving to other locators of its own while every list is taken reuses the list it leaves.
The SEDP builtin readers are reliable StatefulReaders matched from SPDP: they request lost announcements, reassemble fragmented ones, and apply disposals from the owning participant.
The SEDP builtin writers and readers are matched with a discovered participant at its metatraffic unicast locators; a participant that announces none is not matched in either direction.
Endpoint matching requires identical topicName and typeName.
RELIABLE readers are only compatible with RELIABLE writers.
Writer durability must be greater than or equal to reader durability for compatibility.
Participant endpoint removal dissolves existing matches, and rediscovered endpoints can rematch cleanly.
SEDP PL_CDR parameter list parsing skips unknown PIDs while continuing to parse known fields.
Discovered endpoint data requires PID_ENDPOINT_GUID for valid endpoint identity.
A matched remote endpoint that re-announces a different unicastLocatorList is matched again at the new locators, and no match refers to the locators it left.
